keyframe_review.note: 22,847 km2 for 1385-1406. The page gives no area, only that Moravia was 'about half' the size of Bohemia proper, so the check is loose but within a factor of two. The Cliopatria Kingdom of Bohemia shape for 1385-1414 (106,270 km2) leaves Moravia out (4 border cells of the gazetteer's Moravia; the 1384 and 1415 Bohemia shapes hold 64), so Cliopatria draws the margraviate as a separate state only in 1385-1414. The page says Jobst 'inherited the Margraviate in 1375, ruled autonomously'; why Cliopatria starts in 1385 is not on the pages opened. The shape reaches into modern Austria (the page does not mention it) and is larger than the gazetteer's 'Moravia' region (16,438 km2, 65 cells).

Same 22,847 km2 outline as 1385-1406. Prokop's share ended in 1405 (page: Jobst 'ruled with his brothers John Sobieslaus (until 1382) and Prokop (until 1405)') but no border change is dated 1407; the split looks like a data artefact. Jobst died on 18 January 1411 (Jobst page) and the page lists no margrave for 1411-1419, so the Cliopatria years 1411-1414 are not explained by the pages opened.

region.text: the Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo principalities merged

ledger.note: 1182: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa has the Margraviate of Moravia created. The page: 'In 1182, the Margraviate was created at the behest of Emperor' Frederick Barbarossa, by merging the Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo principalities (infobox 'Established: 1182'). The region is the dossier's reading of the three principalities.

1310: the House of Luxembourg takes the margraviate. The page lists John (1310-1333), son of Emperor Henry VII, and says Moravia 'was ruled by the House of Luxembourg from the extinction of the Přemyslid dynasty until 1437'. Treated as a dynasty change within the same state.

1423: Albert V of Austria, Sigismund's son-in-law, becomes margrave (table 1423-1439); the first Habsburg margrave since Rudolf I of Habsburg in 1306-1307. The page also says the Luxembourgs ruled 'until 1437', a mild disagreement.

region.text: Moravia was occupied by the Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus

ledger.note: 1469: Matthias Corvinus occupies Moravia. The page: 'In 1469, Moravia was occupied by the Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus'. Cliopatria moves Moravia into Hungary's shape only in 1475 (and takes it out of Bohemia's).

region.text: settled in the 1479 Peace of Olomouc, whereby Matthias renounced the royal title

ledger.note: 1479: the Peace of Olomouc ends the contest; Matthias renounced the royal title (of Bohemia) and, the page says, retained the rule over the Moravian lands.

region.text: Matthias retained the rule over the Moravian lands

ledger.note: 1479-1490: Moravia is held by Matthias Corvinus as margrave (table 1468-1490). The page does not call it Hungarian land; Cliopatria draws it inside Hungary 1475-1491, hence the loss to the Kingdom of Hungary (confidence 2).

region.text: Moravia returns with Vladislaus II as margrave (table 1490-1516)

ledger.note: 1490: Vladislaus II of Bohemia (Jagiellon) succeeds Matthias Corvinus as margrave. The page gives the table, not an event sentence; Cliopatria keeps Moravia in Hungary to 1491.

1526: Moravia passes to the Habsburgs. The page: 'incorporated into the Habsburg monarchy upon the death of King Louis II in the 1526 Battle of Mohács'; Ferdinand I is margrave 1527-1564. Treated as a dynasty change within the same state (a Habsburg crown land 1526-1804).
1641: the capital moves from Olomouc to Brno (infobox: Olomouc 1182-1641, Brno 1641-1918); no sentence in the text describes the move.

region.text: In 1918 the Margraviate became 'Moravia Land' and later 'Moravia-Silesia Land'

ledger.note: 1918: the Margraviate of Moravia ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1918') and becomes Moravia Land in Czechoslovakia; its autonomy was eliminated in 1949.

wars.name: Hungarian occupation of Moravia and the Peace of Olomouc

zones.text: Moravia occupied by Matthias Corvinus in 1469

wars.outcome: Matthias Corvinus occupied Moravia in 1469; the 1479 Peace of Olomouc settled the dispute, Matthias renouncing the royal title (of Bohemia) and retaining the rule over the Moravian lands.
wars.note: The page names the occupation and the peace but not the campaigns; the war's other belligerent (Vladislaus Jagiellon's Bohemia) is not named on this page, only implied by the renounced royal title.

wars.name: Ottoman raids on Moravia
wars.outcome: Moravia was frequently raided; the page says hundreds of thousands were enslaved and tens of thousands killed. No border changed.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary line or treaty; Moravia is a long-lived land named by its three founding principalities and Cliopatria's outline is approximate.

notes: Margraviate of Moravia, eu-15-i, 2 pages (budget 1-2). (1) Cliopatria's row is only 1385-1414, the page's state lasts 1182-1918 (infobox). The dossier takes the page's life, as the Styria dossier does for its 1180-1918 duchy; only 1385-1414 has Cliopatria shapes, and in every other year Cliopatria draws Moravia inside another state: inside Kingdom of Bohemia 1350-1384 and 1415-1474 and 1492-1528 (64 of the gazetteer's Moravia cells), inside Kingdom of Hungary 1475-1491 (65 cells; Bohemia's 1475-1486 shape of 53,017 km2 has 0). The orchestrator must decide whether to draw Moravia as a Bohemian-crown vassal tint outside 1385-1414 (the Kingdom of Bohemia and Habsburg dossiers then must not draw it twice) or only 1385-1414. No new keyframes were written for the other years because the pages give no boundaries. (2) Why Cliopatria carves Moravia out of Bohemia in 1385-1414 is not on the pages opened; the Margraviate page says only that Jobst 'ruled autonomously'; the Jobst page gives no partition of Moravia, and says nothing of 1385, 1407 or 1414. (3) The page lists no margrave for 1411-1419 (Jobst died 18 January 1411, Sigismund is margrave 1419-1423; Wenceslaus IV is not named). (4) Bohemian vassalage: the infobox says Bohemian Crown 1348-1918, imperial state 1198-1806, Habsburg crown land 1526-1804; these are relations for the kingdom-of-bohemia and holy-roman-empire ledgers, not territory events here. (5) The 1469 occupation and 1479 settlement are written from Moravia's side as contest and loss to Hungary; the Hungary dossier should carry the matching occupation_start / gain, and the Hungary dossier's 1475-1491 shape already includes Moravia. Dates differ: the page says 1469, Cliopatria 1475; Matthias is listed as margrave 1468-1490. (6) Rulers: the page's table stops at Matthias II (1608-1617); the infobox names Charles I (1916-1918); 1617-1916 is not on the page. Dates of Luxembourg rule disagree (page: until 1437; table: Albert V of Austria from 1423). (7) The Mohács date (1526), the 1335 Treaty of Trentschin and the 1288 Colloquium generale are on the page; only 1526 is used in the ledger. (8) Area check: no figure on the page, 'about half' of Bohemia proper; Cliopatria's 22,847 km2 is plausible. The gazetteer's 'Moravia' region is 16,438 km2, smaller than Cliopatria's outline: suggest the gazetteer agent compare it with the historical land (Jihomoravský, Olomoucký, Zlínský, Moravskoslezský and part of Vysočina).
